proposal.utterance: How would you BFO-classify 'the capacity of an institution to repair itself'?

entities.label: InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity
entities.rationale: A capacity is paradigmatically a Disposition in BFO: it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a bearer (here, an institution as a LegalInstitution or material entity) and is internally grounded in the bearer's structural and procedural constitution. It is not a Role (which is externally grounded) and not a mere Quality (which is a static measurable property). 'Capacity to repair itself' is a forward-looking, trigger-realizable property—exactly the profile of BFO Disposition. It would be realized in a self-repair process if and when that process occurs.

relations.rationale: InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016) because it is an internally grounded realizable entity inhering in an institution.

As a specifically dependent continuant (Disposition), instances of InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity must inhere in a bearer—paradigmatically a LegalInstitution. This expresses the generic inheres-in constraint.

open_questions: Should InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity be constrained to inhere specifically in instances of working:LegalInstitution, or in a broader class of institutions (e.g., social organisations that are not legal institutions)?
Is 'self-repair' intended to cover procedural amendment (e.g., constitutional amendment processes), judicial self-correction (e.g., overruling precedent), or both? This may warrant sub-dispositions.
Should a corresponding process class (e.g., 'InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess' as a subclass of BFO_0000015/Process) also be minted to serve as the realization target via BFO_0000054 (realized in)?

Is this capacity meant to be distinct from working:InstitutionalEffectiveness (already in the ontology as a Quality), or is it a determinable of which InstitutionalEffectiveness is a determinate? If so, a subclass or part-of relation may be needed.
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'capacity of an institution to repair itself' is a textbook case of a BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016): it is a specifically dependent continuant that (a) inheres in a single bearer (the institution), (b) is grounded in the internal constitution of that bearer—its procedural rules, amendment clauses, oversight mechanisms—and (c) is realizable, meaning it can be triggered into actualization by appropriate circumstances and would then be realized in a self-repair process (a BFO Process). It is not a Quality because it is not a static measurable property but a forward-directed potentiality. It is not a Role because roles are externally socially conferred, whereas this capacity arises from internal structural features of the institution. The new class InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity is proposed as a subclass of BFO_0000016. It is related to but distinct from the existing working:InstitutionalEffectiveness (a Quality) and working:InstitutionalPersistence (also a Quality), and its realization would participate in a Process not yet minted in the ontology.
